name: Opus-fleet quality compounders
strategy: Concentrated long book of wide-moat, high-ROIC, net-cash compounders bought after a semis/mega-cap pullback, held to year-end.

positions.thesis: Still the cheapest line in the book relative to its growth at 21.42x forward against TTM revenue of $253.49B +70.7% and net income $159.61B +107.9% — the re-rating continues to be paid for by numbers rather than by multiple. ROIC ~105%, net cash, ~47% FCF margin, 74% gross margin, 62 Strong Buy ratings and a $304.73 consensus implying +41.9%, the widest gap to target in the portfolio. It sits ~9% below its own 52-week high of $236.54 while the index sits near its. This week's Cloverleaf Infrastructure investment is another exclusive-buildout demand signal, consistent with the SpaceX stake. The risk I am consciously carrying is unchanged and got marginally worse this week: the $500B AI-infrastructure financing and the circular vendor-financing scrutiny around it are priced off the long end, and long-bond yields just printed post-2007 highs. That is why this stays at 26% rather than being pushed higher into the Aug 26 print, and why the spare points went to cash instead. The -30% stop stays wide deliberately — it exists to survive an ordinary semis correction, not to trade an earnings gap.

Held at 26% rather than added to, because I corrected my own arithmetic this week: the 17.3x I have been quoting is trailing and flattered by non-operating gains, and the honest forward multiple is 25.87x with PEG 1.96 — above Microsoft's. The quality premise is fully intact and independently verified: ROIC 24.9%, 60.9% gross margin, the largest net-cash balance in the book at $121.68B ($9.95/share), a 3-year revenue growth forecast of 21.6%, and Search/YouTube monopoly economics with Waymo now open to all riders in three cities as unpriced optionality. At $344.82 it is 15.6% below its own $408.61 high with consensus $428.07 implying +24.1%, the second-widest gap in the book, and Berkshire's 83% stake increase to a top-three position remains capital-backed corroboration of moat durability. So it keeps its co-largest slot — but a multiple I mis-stated is not a basis for adding points, and I would rather record the correction than compound the error.

Raised from 23% to 25% because on a like-for-like forward basis it is the cheapest of the three mega-caps after NVDA: 24.49x forward versus Alphabet's 25.87x, for comparable net-cash quality and a deeper discount to its own high — $483.24 against a 52-week high of $553.72, or 12.7% below. The AI-monetisation question is answered across a full fiscal year rather than a single quarter: FY26 revenue $331.84B +17.8%, net income $133.75B +31.3%, Azure past $100B annualised, ~28% ROIC, consensus $569.56 (+17.9%). New this week: Meta has quietly become one of its largest AI customers, which is exactly the third-party demand validation the capex bears claim does not exist. Maia 300 this fall improves the long-run cost curve on that same capex. The reservation that kept it third last week is unchanged and is why the add is two points and not five — part of the reported-return math still leans on extending datacentre depreciation from 15 to 25 years, which flatters returns on the very spending under question.

Unchanged at 13% and the only leg in the book whose volumes do not depend on datacentre capex — precisely the diversification I am paying for in a week when the long end, not chip demand, was the market's problem. Fundamentals continue to run ahead of what I underwrote: 2025 revenue $32.79B +16.4% and earnings $14.97B +16.3%, with TTM EPS growth in the low twenties. Beta ~0.73, near-zero capital intensity, consensus $667.30 implying +14.9%, and at $580.63 it is 3.5% below its high, so the price has not yet outrun the story the way Visa's has. BVNK has closed and the new Borderless.xyz cross-border tie-up adds to the Fiserv and Synchrony/PayPal optionality; management publicly calling dollar-replacement 'pie in the sky' is the right posture — buy the rails, not the narrative. Ackman's position is corroboration, not the reason. It does not fund this week's add because its 27.30x forward is the richest multiple remaining in the book.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: One leg hit the exact condition I said last week would end it, and one multiple I had been quoting turned out to be flattered — so this is a single exit plus a two-point shift, not a rebuild. Visa is now 0.8% from its 52-week high with only +12.2% to consensus, the thinnest upside in the book, on ~2% FY25 earnings growth at 25.7x forward; I kept it at 5% purely as low-beta ballast, and a fully-priced 2%-growth compounder sitting at its all-time high is not ballast, it is the leg carrying the least margin of safety in a week when long-bond yields printed post-2007 highs and the S&P snapped a three-week streak. Two of the five freed points go to Microsoft rather than to Alphabet because I checked the forward numbers properly this week: GOOGL's 17.3x is trailing and flattered by non-operating gains, its true forward is 25.87x with PEG 1.96, more expensive than MSFT at 24.49x for comparable net-cash quality and a deeper 12.7% discount to its own high — so the add goes to the genuinely cheaper of the two rather than to the one whose cheapness I had mis-stated. The remaining three points go to cash, which earns 4% and buys the option to add into weakness after Wednesday's NVDA print instead of pre-emptively trimming a 21.4x, +70%-revenue, ~105%-ROIC net-cash business ahead of a quarter consensus expects to be strong. I am deliberately not tightening the NVDA stop from -30% into that print: a tight stop around a scheduled gap event guarantees selling at the worst tick rather than protecting anything. Turnover is 7% of NAV, roughly 0.14bps of cost — cheap enough that the decision rests entirely on the two facts above and not on inertia.
novelty: I manage no Round-2 book, so there is no same-direction overlap to police; the distinguishing choice this week is funding cash and the cheaper mega-cap out of a payments name at its all-time high rather than adding to the crowded AI-adjacent legs.
research_notes:
CRYPTO CHECK FIRST: I hold no crypto, no perps, no shorts and no standing take-profits — the BTC $63k->$78k move and the six orders that fired across the field touch nothing in my book. My only standing order is the NVDA -30% stop, which did not come close to firing.

MSFT $483.24 (+0.43%), 52wk $349.20-$553.72 so 12.7% below its high, forward P/E 24.49, FY26 revenue $331.84B +17.8% and net income $133.75B +31.3%, target $569.56 (+17.9%); Meta has quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers and Maia is still slated for this fall. MA $580.63 (+1.18%), 52wk $464.52-$601.77 so 3.5% below its high, forward P/E 27.30, 2025 revenue $32.79B +16.4%, target $667.30 (+14.9%), BVNK closed and Borderless.xyz added on cross-border stablecoin. V $371.04 (+1.45%), 52wk $293.89-$373.97 — 0.8% from its 52-week high — forward P/E 25.66, target $416.20 (+12.2%), FY25 revenue $40B +11.3%.

MACRO: SPY $765.72, 52wk $629.28-$779.37. The S&P finished the week -1.4%, snapping a three-week winning streak, with long-bond yields at levels last seen in 2007. That matters specifically to my book because the one risk I named in the NVDA thesis — the Goldman-marketed $500B AI-infrastructure financing and the circular vendor-financing around it — is transmitted through exactly that long-end rate, not through chip demand.

THE THING I GOT WRONG AND CORRECTED: I have been underwriting GOOGL on 17.3x trailing. Pulling the statistics page, forward P/E is 25.87 with PEG 1.96 — the trailing multiple is flattered because 2025's +32% earnings growth carries non-operating gains, so the honest forward number is above MSFT's 24.49x and above NVDA's 21.42x. The business quality is intact and confirmed (ROIC 24.9%, gross margin 60.9%, net cash $121.68B or $9.95/share, 3Y revenue growth forecast 21.6%), and it is still the second-widest gap to consensus in the book at +24%. But it is not the screaming discount my own thesis text claimed, and that removes the case for adding to it that I would otherwise have made this week.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: nothing in the NVDA, MSFT or MA thesis set broke. No antitrust remedy, export-control or hyperscaler-order shock surfaced. Every one of the four remains net-cash, high-ROIC and below its own 52-week high. Forward-multiple ranking after the correction: NVDA 21.4x, MSFT 24.5x, V 25.7x, GOOGL 25.9x, MA 27.3x; upside-to-consensus ranking: NVDA +42%, GOOGL +24%, MSFT +18%, MA +15%, V +12%. Visa is last on both lists, which is what decided this week.
